title: Successive internal coefficient mates and normalized scalar units
statement:
Let $\Lambda_0\xrightarrow a\Lambda_1\xrightarrow b\Lambda_2$ be maps of commutative condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and let $f:X\to Y$ be any scheme morphism with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_{i,T}=p_T^*\Lambda_i$ for $i=0,1,2$, $T=X,Y$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use ordinary unbounded internal-module derived categories and their specified $L_{f,i}\dashv F_{f,i}$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. For $ij=01,12,02$ let $D_{ij,T}$ be uncompleted derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], with normalized pullback balancing $\lambda^{ij}:L_{f,j}D_{ij,Y}\cong D_{ij,X}L_{f,i}$ [lem-sfb-internal-scalar-pullback-normalization]. Let $\rho^{ij}:D_{ij,Y}F_{f,i}\to F_{f,j}D_{ij,X}$ be its mate under these specified adjunctions [def-sfb-internal-derived-scalar-comparisons].

There exist natural isomorphisms $\beta_T:D_{12,T}D_{01,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{02,T}$ satisfying the successive universal computation-counit normalization of [def-sfb-internal-derived-scalar-comparisons]. On flat-term K-flat representatives $\beta_T$ sends $(x\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $x\otimes b(s)t$, with inverse $x\otimes t\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes t$. It identifies the composite scalar-extension units with the unit for $ba$. These isomorphisms satisfy the pullback identity
$$\beta_XL_{f,0}\circ D_{12,X}(\lambda^{01})\circ(\lambda^{12}D_{01,Y})=\lambda^{02}\circ L_{f,2}(\beta_Y),$$
where the displayed common target is $D_{02,X}L_{f,0}$ and the common source is $L_{f,2}D_{12,Y}D_{01,Y}$. For every $K\in D(R_{0,X})$ the corresponding direct-image identity is
$$\rho^{02}_K\circ\beta_{Y,F_{f,0}K}=F_{f,2}(\beta_{X,K})\circ\rho^{12}_{D_{01,X}K}\circ D_{12,Y}(\rho^{01}_K)$$
in $D(R_{2,Y})$. The unit compatibility is for the normalized adjunctions with representative unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and thus also fixes the corresponding reduction-unit transposes. For an identity coefficient map these comparisons are the canonical identity comparisons. No flatness of either coefficient map and no invertibility of the direct-image mates on arbitrary inputs are asserted or required.

proof.text: For each scheme T, form the canonical exact-restriction compositor from Mod.comapComp and coefficientMap_comp. Transport the composite specified scalar adjunction along this compositor and take leftAdjointUniq with the specified adjunction for the composite coefficient map. This constructs beta_T without choosing data from an unproved existence theorem. The unit_leftAdjointUniq identity gives exactly the two unit equations. Naturality of the restriction compositor and homEquiv_leftAdjointUniq give the transpose equations.

proof.text: The derived-adjunction unit factorization, followed by the exact-restriction localization isomorphism, identifies the transpose of the scalar computation counit with the ordinary scalar unit on every homotopy-category representative. The ordinary successive balancing comparison is the ordinary left-adjoint uniqueness comparison: its unit identity follows by unfolding ordinaryComp and Mod.extendScalarsComp. Apply normalizedAdjunction_composition and normalizedAdjunction_uniqueness from lem-pur-normalized-adjunction-composition, with the exact restriction factorization, to obtain SuccessiveNormalized. Thus beta_T is normalized by the fixed ordinary balancing isomorphism on whole complexes.

proof.text: Prove the ordinary pullback rectangle by conjugating its left-adjoint isomorphisms to right-adjoint isomorphisms. The conjugate of ordinaryComp is the restriction compositor by the unit equation; the conjugate of pullIso is comapLowerStarIso by its definition. Both right-adjoint pastings have the same underlying module map: after Mod.hom_ext their maps are identities. ConjugateIsoEquiv injectivity gives the ordinary rectangle. Apply additive functors to complexes degree by degree and pass to homotopy classes; the comparison with a composite functor is transported with its canonical target compositor.

proof.text: Compose the two derived rectangle maps with the scalar and geometric computation counits. Naturality of these counits, SuccessiveNormalized, the three PullNormalized hypotheses, and the ordinary rectangle give equality on every homotopy representative. To deduce equality of natural transformations, cancel the given normalized pullback isomorphism and use a K-flat left resolution of a homotopy representative: its localization is invertible, and the scalar computation counit is invertible on that resolving object. Cancellation and naturality give equality after arbitrary postcomposition. The remaining geometric computation counit is invertible because geometric module pullback is exact. This proves pullback pasting without asserting preservation of K-flatness by a scalar word.

proof.text: Transpose both direct-image pastings under the specified final geometric adjunction. The mate-counit equation rewrites each rho. Naturality of the second balancing map and beta_X moves the first geometric counit to the boundary; the pullback rectangle identifies the resulting transposes. Injectivity of the Hom equivalence yields the direct-image equation. This calculation never requires a direct-image mate to be invertible.

proof.text: For an identity coefficient map, use ordinary and derived left-adjoint uniqueness against the identity adjunction transported along the corresponding restriction unitor. The same normalized transpose calculation identifies the derived scalar unitor with its ordinary computation-counit normalization. Conjugating the ordinary scalar compositor shows that either identity factor is the appropriate whiskered unitor. Conjugating the ordinary geometric square shows it is the square of ordinary unitors. Lift these identities degree by degree and use computation-counit naturality and the absolute uniqueness argument of step 4. This gives betaLeft, betaRight and the formula for the identity pullback comparison. Transposition under the geometric adjunction gives its direct-image mate. The identity scalar unit equation is the unit_leftAdjointUniq equation. The argument applies without any nonzero-ring or flatness hypothesis.
